questions.question:
**In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the option corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the "No error" option.**

The CEO has decided to visit all the (1)/ departments of the office tomorrow (2)/ evening to review of the situation. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution: The error lies in the third part of the sentence as the expression ‘**to** review **of** the situation’ represents incorrect sentence construction. The usage of ‘**to** review the situation’ is sufficient as it means to analyse the situation.

**In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the option corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the "No error" option.**

Ashish was listening (1)/ to a radio when (2)/ Sunita arrived. (3)/ No Error (4)

questions.question:
**In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the option corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the "No error" option.**

When the professors are on strike (1)/ and a notice to this effect is pasted on the university gate (2)/ there is no sense to go there. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** '3'** (i.e. the content inside the correct option).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "no sense to go there" is grammatically incorrect. The correct form is "no sense in going there."
 
• The proper idiomatic expression is "no sense in [doing something]," indicating the lack of reason or logic in performing an action.
 
• "Going" is the gerund form required after the preposition "in".
 
• Using "no sense in going there" makes the sentence clearer and more understandable.
 
• "No sense in [verb+ing]" is a commonly accepted phrase in the English language, making it more familiar to readers.
 
• Given the context of professors being on strike, using "no sense in going there" properly conveys the futility of going to the university.

Therefore, the correct answer is** 'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 1) "When the professors are on strike": This part is grammatically correct and provides context.
 
• 2) "And a notice to this effect is pasted on the university gate": This part correctly conveys relevant information.
 
• 4) "No Error": This is not the correct option because there is an error in the sentence.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the word which best expresses the meaning of the given word and click the button corresponding to it.**

Invidious
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Hateful.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The word similar in meaning to **Invidious** is "Hateful".
 
• Let's have a look at the meaning of the words given in the question:-
 
• **Invidious**: Invidious means causing envy or resentment, unfairly discriminating or creating a feeling of animosity.
 
 
• Example: The teacher's **invidious **treatment of certain students led to resentment and conflict in the classroom.
 
 
 
• **Mournful**: Mournful means feeling or expressing sorrow or grief.
 
 
• For example, "The **mournful **sound of the funeral dirge filled the church."
 
 
 
• **Slowly**: Slowly means at a slow pace or rate.
 
 
• For example, "The tortoise moved **slowly **across the finish line, winning the race by a shell."
 
 
 
• **Indifferent**: Indifferent means having no particular interest or sympathy, neither good nor bad.
 
 
• For example, "She was **indifferent **to the outcome of the game, as she didn't really care who won."
 
 
 
• **Hateful**: Hateful means full of hate or malice, causing or deserving intense dislike or animosity.
 
 
• For example, "The **hateful **remarks she made about her colleagues led to her being fired from her job."
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is** Option 4.**

Kanika shall be grateful to you if you (are of help) her now.
questions.solution: The usage of shall indicates that the verb is in the simple future tense **(****Will/Shall + Verb)**. Thus ‘help’ should be in base form and no modal verb is required before it. Thus, option 1 is the best fit answer.

questions.question:
**Below are three alternatives which may be used to improve the sentence by replacing the words given in the brackets. You may choose option 1, 2 or 3. In case no improvement is needed, choose 4.**

Not a word (she spoke) to the unfortunate mother about it.
questions.solution: The sentence construction is incorrect in the given statement. Since the act that took place in the past (as suggested by ‘spoke’) and has been completely finished, the simple past tense should be used. So the sentence should be written as: *Not a word **did she speak** to the unfortunate mother about it.* Since all the options have replaced ‘her’ with ‘they’, option 1 is the correct answer.

• The incorrectly spelt word "exhorbitant" includes an extra 'h', which is not present in the correct spelling.
 
• The 'h' in "exhorbitant" creates a non-standard and incorrect version of the word.
 
• Proper spelling is crucial for clear written communication to avoid misunderstandings.
 
• Recognizing and correcting such spelling errors enhances the quality and professionalism of the text.

Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 2'.

questions.question: Science is both a blessing and a _____.
questions.solution: The passage later mentions that** science has also given terrible instruments. **So besides being a ‘blessing’, science must be a **curse **as well.

questions.question: many things which have made life better and _____,
questions.solution: The concerned part of the sentence talks about the positive aspects of science. So, options 1 and 2 can be eliminated. Between 3 and 4, ‘happier’ is more appropriate because it is in the comparative degree as ‘better’.

questions.question: it has also given terrible instruments of _____.
questions.solution: The concerned part of the sentence talks about the negative aspects of science and ‘destruction’ is the best fit word.

questions.question: discovered and invented many things to _____ pain and cure
questions.solution:
Let’s look at the meanings of the given words:

Aggravate => make a problem worse

Alleviate => reduce

Nurture => care for

Intensity => strength; power

Logically speaking, the discoveries and inventions made through science have **reduced** pain. Thus, option 2 is carries the best fit word. Another clue to find the correct word lies in the same sentence: since science has discovered and invented things to cure terrible diseases (which indicates a positive thing), it would have invented things to reduce pain and not the contrary.

questions.question: enabled man to live a longer and _____ life.
questions.solution: ‘Longer’ and ‘healthier’ are complementary words, so option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: According to the passage, corruption is _____.

options.text: prevalent only in middle east countries

questions.solution: According to the given passage, ‘corruption is **not a new phenomenon** in India. It has been **prevalent in society since ancient times**. Thus, option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Kautilya mentions the pressure of how many types of corruption in his contemporary society?
questions.solution: Kautilya mentions the pressure of** forty** types of corruption in his contemporary society.

questions.question: Perversion of what is not mentioned in the passage?
questions.solution: According to the passage, *corruption implies **perversion of morality, integrity, character** or duty out of mercenary motives.* Option 2 is the correct answer as it has not been mentioned.

questions.question: According to the passage, what all are the manifestation of corruption?
questions.solution: According to the passage, ***Dishonesty****, exploitation, **malpractices**, **scams and scandals** are various manifestations of corruption.* Thus, option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question: What people are averse of due to corruption in India?
